sentences.en: In 1968, George Soy stepped off a plane from Hong Kong and into the San Francisco International Airport.
sentences.zh: 1968年，乔治·索伊走下从香港飞来的飞机，踏入了旧金山国际机场。

sentences.en: It was his first time on American soil.
sentences.zh: 这是他第一次踏上美国的土地。

sentences.en: At 22 years old, he had left his homeland of China and traveled across the ocean to build a new life for himself and his young wife in this land of opportunity.
sentences.zh: 22岁那年，他离开了祖国中国，跨越重洋，来到这片充满机遇的土地，为自己和年轻的妻子开创新的生活。

sentences.en: When immigrants first come to the U.S., and this is such an old trope and an old story, is that you expect, you know, the streets are paved with gold.
sentences.zh: 当移民初到美国时——这是一个非常老套的桥段和故事——人们总会期待，你知道的，街道是用黄金铺成的。

sentences.en: This is Bonnie Soy, George's daughter.
sentences.zh: 这是邦妮·索伊，乔治的女儿。

sentences.en: She's also the author of a book about American Chinatowns.
sentences.zh: 她也是一本关于美国唐人街书籍的作者。

sentences.en: Even today, Chinese people still call San Francisco Gamsan, meaning Gold Mountain.
sentences.zh: 即使在今天，华人依然称旧金山为“金山”，意为黄金之山。

sentences.en: This is where you find your fortune, in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 这就是你在旧金山寻找财富的地方。

sentences.en: George Soy's very first stop in San Francisco, his very first stop in America, like generation upon generation of Chinese immigrants before him, was San Francisco's Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 乔治·索伊在旧金山的第一站，也是他踏入美国的第一站，就像在他之前的几代中国移民一样，是旧金山的唐人街。
但他并没有留下深刻的印象。

sentences.en: To George, San Francisco's Chinatown felt out of date.
sentences.zh: 对乔治来说，旧金山的唐人街感觉过时了。

sentences.en: All the things he saw in Chinatown, these pagoda roofs, these dragon gates, these flourishes that, you know, to us signal China and Chineseness.
sentences.zh: 他在唐人街看到的一切，那些宝塔式的屋顶、龙门，以及那些在我们看来象征着中国和中国风的装饰。

sentences.en: They were things that he actually hadn't seen back in China for years and years and years, and they were not used in that architectural vernacular back there.
sentences.zh: 这些东西他其实在中国已经很多年没见过了，而且那里的建筑语言中也并未使用这些元素。

sentences.en: And so he wondered how Chinatown in this, you know, really supposedly modern America was, why did it feel older than the oldest parts of Hong Kong where he'd grown up?
sentences.zh: 所以他感到纳闷，在这个所谓的现代美国，为什么唐人街感觉比他长大的香港最古老的地方还要老旧？

sentences.en: Because it was designed that way.
sentences.zh: 因为它是被刻意设计成那样的。
那是制片人切尔西·戴维斯。

sentences.en: For George Soy and many other Chinese immigrants, San Francisco's Chinatown, and the Chinatowns in a lot of American cities, they don't look much like the China they know.
sentences.zh: 对于乔治·索伊和许多其他中国移民来说，旧金山的唐人街，以及许多美国城市的唐人街，看起来并不像他们所熟悉的中国。

sentences.en: It looks like a bit of a movie set, actually.
sentences.zh: 实际上，它看起来有点像电影布景。

sentences.en: It's so out of context to anything else next to it on either side.
sentences.zh: 它与周围任何其他建筑都格格不入。
那是电影制作人费利西亚·洛。

sentences.en: She made a documentary about San Francisco's Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 她制作了一部关于旧金山唐人街的纪录片。

sentences.en: Walking around Chinatown together, we passed Bank of America ATMs guarded by gold dragons, shops with neon-lit names like Heart of Shanghai, selling paper fans and plastic buddhas,
sentences.zh: 我们一起走在唐人街，经过了被金龙守护的美国银行自动取款机，经过了挂着霓虹灯招牌如“上海之心”的商店，店里卖着纸扇和塑料佛像，

sentences.en: and towering four-story bazaars crowned with little pagodas.
sentences.zh: 还有耸立着、顶端装饰着小宝塔的四层集市。

sentences.en: But Chinatown hasn't always looked this way.
sentences.zh: 但唐人街并非一直都是这个样子。

sentences.en: In fact, before the massive earthquake that leveled San Francisco in 1906, Chinatown looked like most of the other neighborhoods in San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在1906年夷平旧金山的大地震之前，唐人街看起来和旧金山的其他街区没什么两样。

sentences.en: Rows of brick homes done up with Victorian Italianate facades.
sentences.zh: 一排排砖房，装饰着维多利亚意大利风格的门面。

sentences.en: The only thing you recognize as Chinatown are the people in it and the Chinese signs instead of American signs.
sentences.zh: 唯一能让你认出那是唐人街的，只有里面的人和中文招牌，而不是美国招牌。

sentences.en: That's Phil Choi, a retired architect and historian of Chinese American culture.
sentences.zh: 那是菲尔·崔，一位退休建筑师和美籍华人文化历史学家。

sentences.en: He grew up in San Francisco's Chinatown and still lives there today.
sentences.zh: 他在旧金山唐人街长大，至今仍住在那里。

sentences.en: He says it's not like Chinese immigrants in SF had strong opinions either way about their neighborhood's Victorian flourishes.
sentences.zh: 他说，并不是旧金山的中国移民对他们街区的维多利亚式装饰有什么强烈的看法。

sentences.en: They just didn't have much choice when it came to where they lived.
sentences.zh: 当谈到居住地时，他们根本没有太多选择。

sentences.en: After arriving in America, they moved into the old homes that white people had abandoned for greener pastures.
sentences.zh: 抵达美国后，他们搬进了白人为了追求更好生活而遗弃的旧房子里。

sentences.en: Basically, the Chinese didn't have time to really pay attention to the architecture or creating Chinese architecture.
sentences.zh: 基本上，华人没有时间去真正关注建筑，或者去创造中式建筑。

sentences.en: The basic desire was to make a living.
sentences.zh: 最基本的愿望就是谋生。

sentences.en: And making a living was easier said than done if you were Chinese in early 20th century San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 如果你是20世纪初旧金山的华人，谋生说起来容易做起来难。

sentences.en: Since the 1860s, Chinese immigrants had been a convenient scapegoat for nationwide job shortages.
sentences.zh: 自19世纪60年代以来，中国移民一直是全国就业短缺的替罪羊。

sentences.en: The result was federal legislation like the 1882 Chinese Exclusion Act,
sentences.zh: 结果就是出台了像1882年《排华法案》这样的联邦立法，

sentences.en: which barred the vast majority of Chinese people from entering the states and made it impossible for Chinese already in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 该法案禁止绝大多数华人进入美国，并使已经在美的华人不可能

sentences.en: In San Francisco, racist housing policies made it almost impossible for people of Chinese heritage to live outside of Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 在旧金山，种族主义住房政策使得华裔几乎不可能在唐人街之外居住。

sentences.en: And when they did set foot outside the 15 square blocks of the Chinese enclave, it was at the risk of physical violence.
sentences.zh: 而当他们踏出这15个街区的华人聚居区时，往往面临着身体暴力的风险。

sentences.en: So the self-contained world of Chinatown served as a desperately needed refuge for Chinese San Franciscans.
sentences.zh: 因此，自给自足的唐人街世界成为了旧金山华人急需的避难所。

sentences.en: But in 1906, that refuge would be eviscerated by a double whammy of a disaster.
sentences.zh: 但在1906年，这个避难所将遭受双重灾难的摧毁。

sentences.en: Early in the morning of April 18th of that year, San Franciscans woke up to a 7.8 magnitude earthquake.
sentences.zh: 那年4月18日清晨，旧金山人从7.8级大地震中惊醒。

sentences.en: It was the biggest quake in the city's recorded history.
sentences.zh: 这是该市有记录以来最大的地震。

sentences.en: But those violent tremors were just the beginning.
sentences.zh: 但那些剧烈的震动仅仅是个开始。

sentences.en: Because the earthquake shattered the city's gas means.
sentences.zh: 因为地震震碎了城市的煤气管道。

sentences.en: And the gas that leaked out, somewhere it connected with a spark.
sentences.zh: 泄漏出来的煤气在某处接触到了火花。

sentences.en: The massive fires that resulted lasted for three days and destroyed about 500 city blocks.
sentences.zh: 由此引发的大火持续了三天，摧毁了约500个城市街区。

sentences.en: Chinatown was one of the first neighborhoods to go up and smoke.
sentences.zh: 唐人街是第一批化为灰烬的街区之一。

sentences.en: The safe space for Chinese really is that 15 block radius of the neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 华人真正的安全空间就是那15个街区的范围。

sentences.en: And without it, it becomes a very dangerous situation.
sentences.zh: 而失去了它，情况就变得非常危险。

sentences.en: Andrea Davies is a historian at the Stanford Humanities Center.
sentences.zh: 安德烈亚·戴维斯是斯坦福大学人文中心的历史学家。

sentences.en: But before her career in academia, she was in a slightly different line of work.
sentences.zh: 但在学术生涯之前，她从事过一份稍微不同的工作。

sentences.en: I was a San Francisco firefighter for about five years.
sentences.zh: 我曾做过大约五年的旧金山消防员。

sentences.en: And so my first assignment was Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 我的第一个任务地点就是唐人街。

sentences.en: Fighting fires in that neighborhood later led Davies to write a social history of the 1906 catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 在那个街区灭火的经历，后来促使戴维斯撰写了一部关于1906年大灾难的社会史。

sentences.en: She says that in the wake of the disaster, newspapers peddled this feel-goody story that the SF quake and fire were social equalizers.
sentences.zh: 她说，灾难发生后，报纸散布了一种令人感觉良好的故事，称旧金山地震和火灾是社会均衡器。

sentences.en: That the shared experience of suffering united San Franciscans of all colors and creeds, man helping man, and so on.
sentences.zh: 称共同的苦难经历团结了所有肤色和信仰的旧金山人，人们互帮互助，等等。

sentences.en: But while white man may have helped white man, no one was helping the Chinese.
sentences.zh: 但虽然白人可能帮助了白人，却没有人帮助华人。

sentences.en: And in fact, the racism against them only intensified.
sentences.zh: 事实上，针对他们的种族主义反而加剧了。

sentences.en: I call it heightened post-disaster racism.
sentences.zh: 我称之为灾后加剧的种族主义。

sentences.en: You could see this heightened racism happening on at least two levels.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到这种加剧的种族主义至少在两个层面上发生。

sentences.en: First, with individual white San Franciscans.
sentences.zh: 首先，是针对个人的白人旧金山居民。

sentences.en: The built environment keeps everyone in their place.
sentences.zh: 建筑环境让每个人都各安其位。

sentences.en: And that's what gets erased on April 18th, 1906.
sentences.zh: 而这正是1906年4月18日被抹去的东西。

sentences.en: So if you're an elite white San Franciscan, you don't have to see the residents of Chinatown unless you go there.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你是旧金山的精英白人，除非你去那里，否则你不必见到唐人街的居民。

sentences.en: As the Chinese are leaving their homes in desperation, they're being yelled at to get out and don't turn back.
sentences.zh: 当华人们绝望地离开家园时，他们被大声呵斥离开，不准回头。

sentences.en: And according to Davies, it wasn't just private citizens who were guilty of that heightened racism.
sentences.zh: 据戴维斯说，不仅是普通公民犯了那种加剧的种族主义，

sentences.en: Because the second place that the fire spurred a flare-up in racism was in how the recovery efforts were managed.
sentences.zh: 因为火灾引发种族主义激增的第二个地方，在于救援工作的管理方式。

sentences.en: The fire department did very little to stop it in Chinatown, and in fact made it worse.
sentences.zh: 消防部门在唐人街几乎没有采取任何灭火行动，实际上反而让情况变得更糟。

sentences.en: And the water mains have broken, so there is not enough water to fight the fires.
sentences.zh: 而且水管破裂了，所以没有足够的水来扑灭火灾。

sentences.en: As if you look at Chinatown, which is nestled right against Nob Hill, where all the elite mansions are,
sentences.zh: 如果你看看紧邻诺布山的唐人街，那里住着所有的精英豪宅，

sentences.en: all the water goes, directed by the mayor, to save Nob Hill.
sentences.zh: 所有的水都被市长指挥去拯救诺布山了。

sentences.en: And all the dynamite goes into Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 而所有的炸药都被用在了唐人街。

sentences.en: At the time, fire departments would dynamite buildings to keep fire from spreading.
sentences.zh: 当时，消防部门会用炸药炸毁建筑物以防止火势蔓延。

sentences.en: But the fire department used the wrong kind of dynamite, and Chinatown burned all the faster.
sentences.zh: 但消防部门用了错误的炸药，结果唐人街烧得更快了。

sentences.en: In the following days, as the embers of Chinatown cooled,
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几天里，随着唐人街的余烬冷却，

sentences.en: the Chinese found themselves homeless and newly vulnerable in hostile streets.
sentences.zh: 华人们发现自己无家可归，在充满敌意的街道上变得更加脆弱。

sentences.en: But things were about to get worse.
So many of the city's political and business leaders were actually excited about this social equalizing disaster
sentences.zh: 该市许多政治和商业领袖实际上对这场社会均衡灾难感到兴奋，

sentences.en: because it eliminated Chinatown, and they thought, we'll never rebuild it.
sentences.zh: 因为它消灭了唐人街，他们认为，我们永远不会重建它。

sentences.en: Before the quake, many whites had seen the Chinese neighborhood as a gomorrah of opium dens, prostitution, and disease.
sentences.zh: 地震前，许多白人将华人街区视为鸦片烟馆、卖淫和疾病的罪恶之城。

sentences.en: In 1885, City Hall had prepared a municipal report on Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 1885年，市政府曾准备了一份关于唐人街的市政报告。

sentences.en: Pages of documentation listing all the houses of prostitution
sentences.zh: 几页的文件列出了所有的妓院，

sentences.en: and the number of gambling houses and opium dens throughout Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 以及唐人街各处的赌馆和鸦片烟馆的数量。

sentences.en: This reputation for vice had actually created a minor industry of slum tourism in Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 这种恶名实际上在唐人街催生了一个小型贫民窟旅游产业。

sentences.en: Thrill-seeking white people could hire a guide to lead them through scenes of alleged depravity.
sentences.zh: 寻求刺激的白人可以雇佣导游带领他们参观所谓的堕落场景。

sentences.en: They would be taken through dimly lit buildings and shown opium smokers and prostitutes and gambling.
sentences.zh: 他们会被带进昏暗的建筑，观看吸食鸦片者、妓女和赌博。

sentences.en: Evidence suggests that some of these scenes may have actually been staged by the guides themselves.
sentences.zh: 有证据表明，其中一些场景实际上可能是由导游自己安排的。

sentences.en: And one thing that was definitely fake was a widespread rumor
sentences.zh: 而有一件事绝对是虚假的，那就是一个广泛流传的谣言，

sentences.en: that San Francisco's Chinese residents lived in underground tunnels.
sentences.zh: 称旧金山的华人居民住在地下隧道里。

sentences.en: This is what they really believed, that the Chinese lived underground.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们真正相信的，华人住在地下。

sentences.en: On top of all this, Chinatown was right in the middle of choice downtown real estate.
sentences.zh: 除此之外，唐人街正处于市中心黄金地段的中心位置。

sentences.en: Real estate that San Franciscan elites had long wanted for white businesses.
sentences.zh: 那是旧金山精英们长期以来一直想为白人企业争取的房地产。

sentences.en: In fact, two years before the fire,
sentences.zh: 事实上，在火灾发生前两年，

sentences.en: then-Mayor James Phelan had hired an architect to draw up sketches for a new downtown.
sentences.zh: 时任市长詹姆斯·费伦曾聘请一位建筑师绘制新市中心的草图。

sentences.en: The architect they hired, you may have heard of him, Daniel Burnham.
sentences.zh: 他们聘请的建筑师，你可能听说过他，丹尼尔·伯纳姆。

sentences.en: And in his plan, there is no Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 在他的规划中，没有唐人街。

sentences.en: Burnham was a proponent of the City Beautiful movement,
sentences.zh: 伯纳姆是“城市美化运动”的支持者，

sentences.en: an urban planning philosophy popular in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在19世纪末和20世纪初流行的城市规划哲学。

sentences.en: And this idea of City Beautiful, it's very racialized, this view.
sentences.zh: 而这种城市美化的理念，这种观点是非常种族化的。

sentences.en: And the idea is a more beautiful urban environment creates a more beautiful citizen.
sentences.zh: 其理念是，更美丽的城市环境能创造出更美丽的公民。

sentences.en: Like, we want a beautiful city of well-educated citizens, and everyone is white and productive.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我们想要一个由受过良好教育的公民组成的美丽城市，每个人都是白人且富有成效。

sentences.en: And with Chinatown burned to the ground,
sentences.zh: 随着唐人街被烧成平地，

sentences.en: city leaders seized the chance to make that white dream a reality.
sentences.zh: 城市领导人抓住了机会，将那个白人梦想变为现实。

sentences.en: Within a week of the fire, City Hall created a committee dedicated solely to relocating Chinatown.
sentences.zh: 火灾发生后的一周内，市政府成立了一个专门负责搬迁唐人街的委员会。

sentences.en: The group included former mayor James Phelan,
sentences.zh: 该小组成员包括前市长詹姆斯·费伦，

sentences.en: the one who had hired Burnham to draw up those revised drafts of San Francisco.
sentences.zh: 就是那个聘请伯纳姆绘制旧金山修订草图的人。

sentences.en: And so the minute the city goes up in flames,
sentences.zh: 所以就在城市陷入火海的那一刻，

sentences.en: I'm not kidding, I don't think the city's finished burning.
sentences.zh: 我没开玩笑，我觉得城市还没烧完呢。

sentences.en: And James Phelan is telegraphing, Daniel Burnham,
sentences.zh: 詹姆斯·费伦就在给丹尼尔·伯纳姆发电报，

sentences.en: send more reports immediately, get them to the hands of the city leaders and business leaders.
sentences.zh: 立即发送更多报告，把它们送到城市领导人和商业领袖手中。

sentences.en: Here's our plan, we can rebuild, here's the perfect city.
sentences.zh: 这是我们的计划，我们可以重建，这是完美的城市。

sentences.en: The plan for that perfect city booted the Chinese all the way to Hunter's Point,
sentences.zh: 那个完美城市的计划将华人一路赶到了亨特角，

sentences.en: a region on the edge of town.
It's where the city's slaughterhouses were.
sentences.zh: 那是城市屠宰场所在地。

sentences.en: But it wasn't long before the Chinese residents found out about the plan.
sentences.zh: 但没过多久，华人居民就发现了这个计划。

sentences.en: And they fought back, and I think they fought back very intelligently.
sentences.zh: 他们进行了反击，而且我认为他们反击得非常聪明。

sentences.en: They got China's empress dowager, Sushi, involved.
sentences.zh: 他们让中国的慈禧太后参与了进来。

sentences.en: She sent her consul general from Washington to meet with San Francisco officials.
sentences.zh: 她派出了驻华盛顿的总领事与旧金山官员会面。

sentences.en: But the coup de grace was financial.
sentences.zh: 但致命一击是经济上的。

sentences.en: For decades, San Francisco had been a key hub for trade with China.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，旧金山一直是与中国贸易的关键枢纽。

sentences.en: So, a group of the city's top Chinese business owners wrote to the current mayor
sentences.zh: 因此，该市一群顶尖的华人企业主写信给现任市长，

sentences.en: in a language San Francisco officials could easily understand.
sentences.zh: 用旧金山官员容易理解的语言。

sentences.en: And so on the business level of the negotiation was,
sentences.zh: 所以在谈判的商业层面上，意思是，

sentences.en: okay, you don't want us to come back?
sentences.zh: 好吧，你们不想让我们回来？

sentences.en: We're not going to Hunter's Point.
So there's a panic of a loss of revenue for the city.
sentences.zh: 所以城市陷入了收入损失的恐慌中。

sentences.en: And that was a loss that city leaders couldn't take.
sentences.zh: 那是城市领导人无法承受的损失。

sentences.en: Less than a month after the quake,
sentences.zh: 地震发生不到一个月后，
